title: Metasurface to raise $9.82 mil via IPO placement of 18 mil new shares at 54 cents each
article:
Metasurface Technologies Holdings Limited (Metasurface) will be placing out 18 million new shares at 54 cents each for the upcoming dual primary listing on Catalist.

Shares of Metasurface has already been listed on the GEM board of the Hong Kong stock exchange since July 2024.

Post placement, Metasurface’s market capitalisation will be around $90 million.

Net proceeds from this placement will be used to for business expansion such as acquiring more advanced machinery and software and for general working capital.

Application will close on Nov 2, 12pm and trading will commence on Nov 4, 9am.

UOB Kay Hian is the sponsor, issue manager and placement agent for Metasurface’s placement.

title: Wall Street choppy as mega-cap losses offset chip gains before Fed decision

Pimco offloads billions in AI debt just in time to skirt losses — Bloomberg
article:
(Oct 28): Investing giant Pacific Investment Management Co (Pimco) helped supercharge the artificial intelligence (AI) debt boom with billions of dollars in lending in 2025 — and has cut positions just in time to skirt losses and eke out a profit.

With a series of well-timed sales, interest rate hedges and a decision to skip later AI bond deals, Pimco has so far managed to duck the billions of dollars in hits that fixed-income investors now face after a flood of debt overwhelmed the market and sent prices tumbling.

Pimco’s most notable AI investment came last year, when it anchored a debt deal with about US$18 billion that allowed Meta Platforms Inc to build a massive Louisiana data centre project without weighing down its own balance sheet. The financing became a template for future deals, including the firm’s investment in Oracle Corp’s massive data centre campus in Michigan.

Some half a trillion dollars of borrowing later, the bond giant that helped kick off the binge has pulled back on some of its largest positions, in some cases months after buying, according to people familiar with the matter.

In addition to the roughly US$18 billion of Meta-related debt, Pimco backed US$10 billion of the Oracle deal across its funds, Bloomberg reported at the time. It now holds about 50% less of each position, filings show, having sold the remaining parts when the notes were trading higher, the people said, asking not to be identified discussing confidential information.

After initially gaining, the bonds backing Oracle’s Michigan development — issued at a discounted price of 98.7 cents on the dollar — have since dropped to around 88 cents, according to the industry’s price-reporting system, known as Trace. As a so-called anchor investor, Pimco bought the bonds at a significant discount to the official price, minimizing potential losses, according to a person familiar with the matter.

See also: S&P 500 churns in countdown to Fed, tech earnings

In the case of the Meta debt — known as Beignet — Pimco flipped about US$3 billion of the bonds six to eight months after buying, when the debt was trading above par, one of the people said.

In the initial months after pricing, the debt rallied to more than 110 cents on the dollar.

The moves reveal how a large investor is taking quick action to protect itself against losses, and is walking a fine line between attempting to profit from the AI boom while navigating the risks that lie in the vast sums spent on its development.

See also: US stocks rise in run-up to tech results as oil falls

Despite reducing its positions, the asset manager is still among the largest holders of the multibillion-dollar data centre financings in Michigan and Louisiana. Prices on both of those bonds have fallen in recent weeks.

The bond giant has become one of most vocal critics of the private credit boom, warning of loose lending standards as the industry has ballooned to more than US$1.8 trillion. And it’s recently been more cautious on artificial intelligence bets.

For example, the firm opted not to invest in a jumbo debt deal for Broadcom Inc and Anthropic PBC earlier this year, and passed on deals such as SoftBank Group Corp’s roughly US$11 billion junk bond and Oracle-tied loans for a New Mexico data centre, the people said.

Still, the firm bought a US$4 billion slice of a huge SpaceX financing deal that will help expand its AI ambitions, Bloomberg reported Monday. Such investments have put Pimco alongside alternative-asset behemoths including Blackstone Inc and Apollo Global Management Inc in helping shape how some of the industry’s biggest debt financings are structured.

Other large AI debt deals, including Broadcom’s, have lost value in recent weeks. Those bonds are being quoted for around 96 cents on the dollar.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Shares of Meta slumped last week after chief executive officer Mark Zuckerberg told investors the company would bet even more aggressively on AI.

The price of insuring Meta debt against default over the next five years rose to a record last week as investors braced for the company to take on more debt or related liabilities.

AI companies have telegraphed their enormous spending plans for data centres and chip development, causing investors to call out the exuberance over the technology and compare it to the run-up to the dot-com crash.

Billionaire Citadel founder Ken Griffin said last week that companies are still confronting the implications of AI, including how much they’ll spend on the technology and how it might impact the economy.

Later last week, Blackstone president Jon Gray took a different tack, saying investors don’t need to fear that the AI boom will turn into a bubble.

“When you think about a bubble, you think about building capacity and then hoping the demand comes,” Gray said in an interview with Bloomberg Television, after the firm reported quarterly results. “With AI, you’re building capacity, and you’re hoping you can keep up with the demand.”

title: S&P 500 churns in countdown to Fed, tech earnings
article:
(Oct 28): Wall Street investors refrained from making big moves before key tech results and a Federal Reserve decision that will shape the outlook for markets through the remainder of 2026.

Following back-to-back gains, the S&P 500 fluctuated. A gauge of chipmakers rose for a fourth straight day. The artificial-intelligence (AI) trade that has powered the bull run will face a fresh test when Microsoft Corp and Alphabet Inc report earnings later on Wednesday. Another advance in oil prices stoked inflation concerns, sending benchmark Treasury yields higher.

With US policymakers expected to hold rates steady, attention will shift to any clues on the path of monetary policy. If they do stay put, Fed chair Kevin Warsh could face pressure to explain the rationale for not acting now after officials voted unanimously last month to raise rates to address burgeoning inflation.

Projections released last month signalled they supported one additional hike this year. The Fed will release a post-meeting statement at 2pm in Washington, and Warsh is scheduled to hold a press conference 30 minutes later.

“While more Fed hikes remain in store in the coming months, we think the current backdrop remains favorable,” said Ulrike Hoffmann-Burchardi at UBS Chief Investment Office. “We do not believe a measured tightening cycle will derail the US economy.”

See also: US stocks rise in run-up to tech results as oil falls
• OpenAI intends to buy AI computing chips from Alphabet Inc’s Google, according to a person familiar with the matter.
• SK Hynix Inc unveiled plans to return about US$45 billion more to shareholders after profit surged a stronger-than-expected seven-fold.
• GE Vernova Inc agreed to pay US$9 billion to acquire Trench Group. The company also raised its sales guidance.
• Vertiv Holdings Co expects 2026 sales to almost triple since 2021 as it benefits from soaring demand for data-center equipment.
• Robinhood Markets Inc dropped on disappointing earnings. JPMorgan Chase & Co trimmed its price target, noting a decline in customer engagement.
• Boston Scientific Corp sank after the medical-device maker’s profit outlook fell short of the average estimate.

See also: Tech stocks power Wall Street gains as oil falls

Some of the main moves in markets:
• The S&P 500 rose 0.1% as of 10:24 a.m. New York time
• The Nasdaq 100 was little changed
• The MSCI World Index was little changed
• The euro was little changed at US$1.1127
• The Japanese yen fell 0.2% to 158.21 per dollar

• The yield on 10-year Treasuries advanced two basis points to 5.02%
• Germany’s 10-year yield was little changed at 3.36%

title: Bank of Canada raises rates to 2.5%, says more could be needed
article:
(Oct 28): The Bank of Canada (BOC) hiked interest rates to ward off upside inflation risks posed by higher energy prices, and said it may need to raise borrowing costs further.

Policymakers led by governor Tiff Macklem raised the benchmark overnight rate to 2.5% on Wednesday, the first increase in more than three years. The hike was expected by markets and was the consensus of Bay Street economists in a Bloomberg survey.

“Governing Council decided to increase the policy rate to reduce the risk that continuing high energy prices spread broadly to the prices of other goods and services,” the bank said in its statement.

“There could be a need to increase the policy rate further, but given uncertainties, Governing Council agreed to proceed carefully.”

Since September, the central bank has been increasingly worried that higher oil prices resulting from the conflict in the Middle East would bleed through to the prices of other goods and services.

Now, the bank expects yearly inflation won’t return to the 2% target until the middle of 2028.

See also: French consumer confidence drops to 13-year low following riots

“With the outlook for inflation substantially higher and the economy showing resilience, an increase in the policy rate is needed to reduce the risk that elevated energy prices could spill over and become generalised inflation,” Macklem said in prepared remarks.

The loonie was little changed after the BOC decision, trading at C$1.4046 per US dollar. It has gained about 1.3% against the US currency in October so far. The price action in Canada rates was also muted with two-year yields edging lower, but remaining within the day’s range.

See also: Germany’s business outlook in October unexpectedly improves for sixth month

In the monetary policy report accompanying the decision, policymakers made major upward revisions to their inflation forecast, and now expect the yearly change in the consumer price index to be 3.1% in 2027, from its previous 2.0% projection.

“The main argument for an increase was that energy prices are higher, they are expected to remain higher, and costs pressures are building,” Macklem said. Governing Council agreed there was “less scope for monetary accommodation,” he said.

But Macklem also said the central bank had discussed holding interest rates steady. The main arguments for a pause include that increased inflation is concentrated in energy, there’s still slack in the economy and the tariff dispute with the US will weigh on growth, he said.

“Governing Council agreed we would take future decisions one meeting at a time,” Macklem said.

There’s no resolution in sight for the war in Iran, and oil prices are almost as high as they were in the early weeks of the conflict. As of Wednesday morning, Brent crude was trading just below US$115 a barrel.

Charles St-Arnaud, chief economist at Servus Credit Union, said he’d be surprised if the bank didn’t hike again in December, despite Macklem’s non-committal language. Pausing “would require weakening economic activity or slower inflation than expected,” he said.

In the monetary policy report, the bank provided insights from Prima, its new forecasting tool. The model points to higher input costs such as energy causing more persistent increases for consumers, as those producer prices have filtered through the economy.

To stay ahead of Singapore and the region’s corporate and economic trends, click here for Latest Section

Officials also raised Canada’s growth outlook and expect the economy to expand 1% in 2026, and 2% in 2027 and 2028. Previously, the bank saw growth at 0.7% in 2026, and 1.8% in 2027 and 2028. The bank is no longer forecasting core inflation pressures.

The bank attributed the higher growth in part to federal measures, including Prime Minister Mark Carney’s so-called productivity mega deduction and the ramp-up of major projects.

Despite that strength, the economy is still struggling to find its footing. The labour market has shed jobs two months in a row, while US tariffs and reduced immigration are creating headwinds for some sectors. The housing market is also weak.

Macklem and senior deputy governor Carolyn Rogers will speak to reporters at 10.30am Ottawa time.

title: US trade gap jumps to most since March 2025 on capital goods
article:
(Oct 28): The US merchandise-trade deficit widened in September to the largest since March 2025 amid an ongoing surge in imports of capital goods.

The shortfall in goods trade grew 2.1% from the prior month to US$134.9 billion, Commerce Department data showed on Wednesday. The median estimate in a Bloomberg survey of economists was for a US$130.2 billion deficit. The figures aren’t adjusted for inflation.

The value of merchandise imports rose 2.4%, while exports advanced 2.6%. Imports of capital goods — a category that includes the computers and accessories, semiconductors and telecommunications equipment fuelling the artificial intelligence (AI) buildout — jumped 7.5%.

Wednesday’s figures suggest capital goods imports continued to weigh on the trade balance in September amid a rush to outfit data centres with components produced abroad. The category has been the primary driver of the sharp deterioration in the deficit over the last year as the AI investment boom has picked up in pace.

“So much of the hardware that the tech companies need is coming from overseas, driving a massive widening in the trade gap,” Stephen Stanley, the chief US economist at Santander Capital Markets, said in a note.

See also: US consumer confidence rises for first time in four months

Capital goods exports rose 5.4% last month, according to the report, while exports of consumer goods advanced 6.5%. Exports of food, feeds and beverages jumped 12.8%. Exports of industrial supplies — a category which includes petroleum products and volatile nonmonetary gold trade — fell 1.6%.

Meanwhile, figures on retail inventories, released alongside the goods trade data, rose 0.3%. Wholesale inventories increased 0.6%.

The trade and inventories data will help inform the government’s estimate of third-quarter gross domestic product. Prior to the latest merchandise trade figures, the Federal Reserve Bank of Atlanta’s GDPNow model saw net exports reducing GDP growth by 2.86 percentage points. In the second quarter, they subtracted 1.1 percentage points from GDP.

See also: US new home sales fall amid surge in mortgage rates

“The massive drag on GDP growth from net trade in 3Q likely will be partly offset by a very big jump in equipment investment, and particularly computer equipment investment,” Oliver Allen, a senior US economist at Pantheon Macroeconomics, said in a note. “At least some of the import surge also likely will show up in inventories. That latest data, however, suggests that this offset will be modest.”

More complete monthly trade figures that include the balance on the services account and inflation-adjusted numbers on merchandise trade are due on Nov 4. Separate data published earlier this month showed September saw a 1.1% increase in import prices and a 2.2% rise in export prices.

title: MLT to redevelop two adjacent Changi South properties into a Grade A warehouse for $141 mil
article:
Mapletree Logistics Trust plans to spend $141 million to redevelop the adjacent 9 and 15 Changi South Street 2 into a modern five-storey, Grade A ramp-up warehouse.

When completed in 2Q 2029, the Changi South redevelopment will be the fifth redevelopment project in Singapore undertaken by MLT.

Located within Singapore’s Changi (South) International LogisPark, the new facility will be MLT's first Grade A ramp-up warehouse in eastern Singapore, to better support air cargo customers.

The new five-storey facility will provide almost 500,000 square feet of gross floor area, 34% more than the two existing warehouses.

Jean Kam, CEO of the manager, says that Singapore is MLT’s largest core market and MLT remains focused on rejuvenating and growing its portfolio here.

"This redevelopment is well-positioned to meet the growing demand for modern, high-specification logistics space, given the limited supply of Grade A ramp-up warehouses in the Changi area.

See also: Mapletree Industrial Trust to pay 2QFY2027 distribution of 2.97 cents per unit, down 6.6% y-o-y

"By intensifying the use of the site, we are unlocking greater value from the assets while enhancing the quality and competitiveness of MLT’s portfolio," says Kam.

Separately, MLT has reported DPU of 1.816 cents for its 2QFY2027, compared to 1.815 cents distributed in the year-earlier quarter. This brings its half-year payout to 3.632 cents, versus 3.627 cents paid for 1HFY2026.

Net property income in 2QFY2027 was $154.8 million, up 1% y-o-y; revenue was up 1.4% to $180 million.

See also: OUE REIT to acquire additional 50% stake in Sydney’s Salesforce Tower for A$539.3 mil

MLT managed to keep its portfolio occupancy at 96.4%. Its overall rental reversion was 2.1% but if China's, which was down 1.7% was excluded, MLT would have achieved 4.2%.

In the current FY ending March 2027, MLT has divested assets worth $243 million, at an average premium to valuation of 3.1%.
